root_idea.summary: The evidence associates هأت with calling for an item to be brought or presented.
root_idea.development: The documented lexical material centers on the imperative forms هاتِ، هاتيا، وهاتوا, including demands for presentation of proof; no further root-level semantic development is established by the supplied sources.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular masculine imperative citation form هَاتِ rather than the internal QAC lemma form.

senses.definition: Bring or present something when called for; in a demand for evidence, bring forth the proof.
senses.usage_conditions: Quranically attested in the imperative plural هاتوا. The lexical paradigm also records the singular and dual imperative forms هاتِ and هاتيا. The requested object may be proof or evidence, as in the construction “bring your proof.”

cautions: The public headword is normalized to the singular masculine imperative هَاتِ, while the QAC group records the Quranic imperative form هَاتُوا.
No Lane or Maqayis evidence is supplied, so broader Classical Arabic branches and a fuller root-level development are not established here.
